T-csg.one_liner: The asset management client business: it develops relationships and delivers investment solutions to institutional and third-party wealth clients worldwide.
talking_points: Goldman's own description names two client types, institutional and third-party wealth, across public and private asset classes [@R1-S10].
Its campus titles pair the name with 'Sales', and one London team under the name does both new business and existing relationships [@R1-S04][@R1-S01].
It has its own management and strategy team running sales budgeting, fundraising projections and Salesforce data governance [@R1-S13].
Matt Gibson is publicly described as head of the group [@R6-S19].
questions_to_ask: How does the group divide work between people who win new clients and people who look after existing ones?
What does the group measure to know a client relationship is healthy, beyond assets?
Which client segment has changed most in the last year, and what did the team do differently?
watch_outs: Do not say 'CSG just means sales' or 'CSG is the sales side and CCG the relationship side': published evidence shows overlap.
Do not quote revenue or headcount for the group: none is disclosed [@R2-S01].

T-ccg.one_liner: A named Goldman group dedicated to retaining, expanding and supporting existing client relationships.
talking_points: Goldman's definition: client service, operational support and risk management, 'partnering closely with the sales team' [@R1-S11].
Published tasks include being main point of contact across portfolio management, trading, operations, legal and compliance, and coordinating account openings, restructures and terminations [@R1-S11].
Whether it sits inside or beside the Client Solutions Group in London is not published.
questions_to_ask: Where does a new mandate pass from the person who won it to the person who looks after it?
What makes an onboarding go well from the client's point of view?
How much investment knowledge does a client coverage analyst need in the first year?
watch_outs: Do not describe it as administrative: the published tasks need investment and operational knowledge.
Do not state how it reports relative to CSG.

T-uk.one_liner: A grouping used in this project for the UK-facing units; not a confirmed Goldman reporting unit.
talking_points: Public evidence supports UK and Ireland institutional and third-party wealth businesses and London-based fiduciary management [@R6-S05][@R1-S17][@R6-S04].
The claim that the UK team is 'the largest by far' has no public support.
Chloe Kipling, now co-head of EMEA Institutional Client Coverage, previously led UK and Ireland institutional [@R6-S02][@R6-S05].
questions_to_ask: How do the UK institutional, wealth and fiduciary teams work together on a client that could use more than one?
What distinguishes UK clients from continental ones in what they ask for?
Which UK client type is growing fastest for the team?
watch_outs: Do not present 'UK team with three sub-teams' as Goldman's structure: OCIO sits in an investing group.
Do not name a current UK institutional head: none is publicly established.

T-uk-inst.one_liner: Coverage of UK pension schemes, local government funds, endowments, charities and other institutions.
talking_points: UK defined benefit schemes are in aggregate surplus (133.7% funded on the PPF measure at end October 2026), so the question is endgame: insure or run on [@R3-S29].
The Pension Schemes Act 2026 eases surplus release and requires defined contribution defaults to reach £25bn by 2030 [@R3-S20].
LGPS pools fell from eight to six and funds must delegate implementation to them [@R3-S21].
Bank Rate rose to 4% on 5 November 2026 [@R3-S31].
In the 2026 cycle a London listing was titled 'Client Solutions Group, UK Institutional Sales' [@R1-S31].
questions_to_ask: With schemes in surplus, what are trustees asking the team for that they were not asking three years ago?
How does the team work with investment consultants on a strategy that has not yet been rated?
How is coverage of LGPS pools different from covering a corporate scheme?
watch_outs: Do not talk about deficits and recovery plans as the main UK pension story.
Do not assume every market change is a product opportunity.
Do not attribute any public mandate to this team: no source does.

T-uk-tpw.one_liner: Sells Goldman funds, ETFs and alternatives to private banks, wealth managers, advisers and multi-managers, who invest for their own clients.
talking_points: Goldman's UK team is 'responsible for new business development' with private banks, wealth managers, financial advisers and multi-managers [@R1-S17].
The reported channel is 'third-party distributed': $714bn of long-term assets at 30 September 2026, globally [@R2-S02].
Thirteen active ETFs were launched in Europe in 2025, and the first evergreen ELTIF 2.0 fund in March 2026 [@R4-S17][@R4-S20].
The Consumer Duty's price-and-value outcome shapes how buyers judge a fund [@R4-S31].
The EMEA head left in April 2026 with no successor publicly named [@R6-S06].
questions_to_ask: After a fund is approved by a wealth manager, what does the team do to help advisers actually use it?
How do conversations change when the product is an active ETF or a semi-liquid private-markets fund?
Which kind of UK intermediary is hardest to reach, and why?
watch_outs: Do not call the end investor the client.
Do not treat an approved-list place as assets won.
Do not name an EMEA or UK and Ireland head.

T-ocio.one_liner: Takes delegated responsibility for running all or part of an institution's portfolio; global, and part of Multi-Asset Solutions.
talking_points: $480bn of OCIO assets globally at 31 March 2026 [@R3-S09].
BAE Systems (about £23bn, 2023): competitive tender, Redington advising trustees, in-house team transferred [@R3-S02].
Shell (about $40bn, 2025): tender overseen by Isio, each fund deciding for itself [@R7-S08].
UK trustees must tender to at least three providers above 20% of assets [@R3-S24].
UK fiduciary fees fell about 27% in five years [@R8-S10].
questions_to_ask: How do coverage teams and the fiduciary management team divide a prospect between them?
What do the largest schemes want from an outsourced provider that smaller ones do not?
How does the team handle the question of using Goldman's own funds inside a client's portfolio?
watch_outs: Do not say OCIO is UK-only or that it always absorbs the client's team.
Do not name the second company from the starting account.
Do not quote an OCIO fee: none is public.

T-consultant.one_liner: Covers the investment consulting firms that advise institutions, rate managers and run selections.
talking_points: Goldman describes it as working with regional institutional sales teams and building a pipeline for them [@R1-S21].
Consultants ran or advised the public UK tenders: Redington (BAE), Isio (Shell), Barnett Waddingham (Calor) [@R3-S02][@R7-S08][@R7-S16].
Consultancy is consolidating, so each research team's rating matters more [@R3-S34].
questions_to_ask: What does it take to get a new strategy rated by a major consultant?
How does the team keep consultant researchers informed between formal reviews?
How has consolidation among consultants changed the work?
watch_outs: Do not describe consultants as salespeople for managers: they are paid by the client.
Named leadership here rests partly on snippet-only sources: use titles cautiously.

T-me.one_liner: Coverage of Gulf and wider Middle East clients, including sovereign investors, from the region and London.
talking_points: Goldman opened a Kuwait office in October 2025 and a Riyadh regional headquarters in December 2025 [@R5-S28][@R5-S29][@R5-S30].
Public sovereign arrangements differ in kind: a $1bn Mubadala account, a non-binding PIF memorandum, a QIA target of $25bn [@R5-S04][@R7-S26][@R7-S28].
2027 CSG listings exist for Dubai and Doha with no stated language requirement [@R1-S07][@R1-S08].
The previous regional head left in September 2025; his team included London staff [@R6-S14].
questions_to_ask: How does covering a sovereign investor differ from covering a pension scheme in what they ask of a manager?
How is coverage split between London and the regional offices?
What do sovereign clients want beyond investment returns, such as co-investment or training?
watch_outs: Do not add headline sovereign numbers together: targets and memoranda are not funded assets.
Do not say Arabic is not required; say no requirement appears in the advertisements read.
Do not name a current regional head.

T-nordics.one_liner: Coverage of Nordic clients from Stockholm, Copenhagen and London, as one integrated team since 2020.
talking_points: In May 2020 institutional sales and third-party distribution merged into one Nordic organisation covering all client types and asset classes [@R5-S26].
That is a counter-example to the idea that every region splits institutional from wealth.
A Nordic role seen in job-advert evidence asked for Swedish, a supported inference only.
questions_to_ask: What made a single integrated team the right model for the Nordics?
Which Nordic client type is most active at the moment?
How much of the coverage is done from London?
watch_outs: Language requirements here are not verified from a primary advert.
No recent Nordic mandate is publicly established.

T-ch.one_liner: Swiss coverage, publicly evidenced as a third-party wealth business with its own head and a London support seat.
talking_points: Patrik Zumstein has led Swiss Third Party Wealth since the start of 2025 [@R4-S07].
A London-based sales-support analyst has been hired for the 'TPW Switzerland team' [@R1-S18].
Language evidence is mixed: a Zurich role requires German, a London support advert listed none [@R5-S06][@R5-S11].
questions_to_ask: How do Swiss private banks' fund selection processes differ from UK wealth managers'?
What is covered from London and what from Zurich or Geneva?
Which products are Swiss intermediaries asking about most?
watch_outs: Do not state that a local language is required or not required: the evidence conflicts.
Swiss institutional coverage leadership is not publicly established.

T-benelux.one_liner: Coverage of Belgian, Dutch and Luxembourg clients; the best-documented continental team, with seats in London and the Netherlands.
talking_points: A London advert (October 2026) says the team does both new business and existing institutional relationships and requires native Dutch [@R1-S01].
NN Investment Partners (2022) brought more than 900 staff and a Dutch client base [@R2-S15].
Thirty Dutch funds with about €542bn had moved to the new pension system by March 2026; deadline 1 January 2028 [@R5-S35].
A fiduciary client, Pensioenfonds Vervoer, ended its mandate in 2010 citing underperformance [@R7-S48].
questions_to_ask: How is the Dutch pension transition changing what funds ask of managers?
How do the London and Hague teams split the work?
What did the NN IP integration change for clients?
watch_outs: This team needs native Dutch: do not present it as a likely seat for an English-only candidate.
NN Group partnership terms are only partly verified.

T-dach.one_liner: German and Austrian coverage, run from Frankfurt in German.
talking_points: The 2027 Frankfurt CSG Institutional Sales listing is for a German speaker [@R1-S05].
Max Bock was named head of Third Party Wealth for Germany and Austria from 1 July 2026 [@R6-S08].
Shell's mandate included $2.8bn in Germany [@R3-S04].
questions_to_ask: How do German institutional vehicles change what a manager has to offer?
Which German client segment is the firm investing most in?
How do the Frankfurt and London teams collaborate?
watch_outs: Not a London team: mention only to show you understand the map.

T-fr.one_liner: French coverage, with third-party wealth run from Paris in French.
talking_points: The 2027 Paris CSG Third Party Wealth listing is for a French speaker [@R1-S06].
A French-speaker advert found belonged to a French third-party wealth sales team, not to Liquidity Solutions [@R5-S09].
questions_to_ask: How does distribution through French banks and insurers differ from the UK?
What is covered from Paris and what from London?
Which wrappers matter most for French intermediaries?
watch_outs: Institutional leadership for France is not publicly established.

T-it.one_liner: Italian coverage from Milan under a long-standing country head.
talking_points: Loredana La Pace is country head for Italy, in post since 2014 and current in 2025–2026 sources [@R6-S11].
Italian distribution runs largely through banks and their networks, a supported inference from general market structure.
questions_to_ask: What makes bank-led distribution in Italy different for an asset manager?
Which products have worked best there?
How does the Milan team use London's product specialists?
watch_outs: Little is publicly established beyond leadership.

T-iberia.one_liner: Spanish and Portuguese coverage, moved from London to Madrid in 2021.
talking_points: Goldman moved its Iberia distribution head and her London team to Madrid in June 2021 [@R6-S13].
Lucía Catalán is managing director for Iberia in 2025–2026 sources [@R6-S12].
questions_to_ask: What changed for clients when the team moved to Madrid?
How do Spanish private banks select funds?
Which other teams have moved closer to their clients?
watch_outs: The structure of the Madrid team is not publicly established.

T-liq.one_liner: Money market funds and short-duration strategies for clients' operating and strategic cash; a global product-line business.
talking_points: Liquidity products were $1,051bn of AUS at 30 September 2026, at about 14bp in 2025 [@R2-S02][@R2-S01].
Clients are financial institutions, hedge funds, institutions, corporates and wealth managers [@R5-S01].
The UK Money Market Funds Regulation is expected to be repealed and replaced by FCA rules [@R5-S32].
Liquidity saw $14bn of net outflows in Q3 2026 while long-term assets grew [@R2-S02].
questions_to_ask: What do treasurers ask about first: yield, access or counterparty risk?
How are UK rule changes affecting sterling fund clients?
How does the team think about tokenised fund shares as collateral?
watch_outs: Do not repeat that everyone speaks French: no public evidence.
Do not treat cash balances as sticky: they follow the client's cash needs.

T-ins.one_liner: Manages insurers' own balance-sheet assets and advises on capital-efficient strategy; a global client vertical.
talking_points: $651bn of general-account assets at 31 December 2025 [@R5-S02].
Goldman's 2026 survey of 434 insurance investment heads: 62% plan to raise private-asset allocations [@R5-S03].
Amended EU Solvency II rules apply from 30 January 2027 [@R5-S39].
The offer runs from partial to full outsourcing plus asset-liability advice [@R5-S02].
questions_to_ask: Which regulatory change is doing most to alter insurers' asset choices?
How does the team work with insurers' own investment staff?
Where do private assets fit when capital charges are considered?
watch_outs: Do not treat insurers as pension funds: capital and accounting rules drive the decision.
EMEA and UK insurance assets are not disclosed.
